**Konrad Zacharias Lorenz** (Austrian German:[[ˈkɔnraːd tsaxaˈriːas ˈloːrɛnts]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Standard_German "Help:IPA/Standard German")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/6/63/De-Konrad_Lorenz.ogg/De-Konrad_Lorenz.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:De-Konrad_Lorenz.ogg "File:De-Konrad Lorenz.ogg"); 7 November 1903– 27 February 1989) was an Austrian [zoologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology "Zoology"), [ethologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethology "Ethology"), and [ornithologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithologist "Ornithologist"). He shared the 1973 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") with [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen") and [Karl von Frisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_von_Frisch "Karl von Frisch"). He is often regarded as one of the founders of modern [ethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethology "Ethology"), the study of animal behavior. He developed an approach that began with an earlier generation, including his teacher [Oskar Heinroth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskar_Heinroth "Oskar Heinroth").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-formemrs-1)

Lorenz studied [instinctive behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinct "Instinct") in animals, especially in [greylag geese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greylag_goose "Greylag goose") and [jackdaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_jackdaw "Western jackdaw"). Working with geese, he investigated the principle of [imprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(ethology) "Imprinting (ethology)"), the process by which some [nidifugous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nidifugous "Nidifugous") birds (i.e. birds that leave their nest early) bond instinctively with the first moving object that they see within the first hours of hatching. Although Lorenz did not discover the topic, he became widely known for his descriptions of imprinting as an instinctive bond. In 1936, he met Tinbergen, and the two collaborated in developing ethology as a separate [sub-discipline of biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology#Branches "Biology"). A _[Review of General Psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review\_of\_General\_Psychology "Review of General Psychology")_ survey, published in 2002, ranked Lorenz the 65th most cited scholar of the 20th century in the technical [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") journals, introductory psychology textbooks, and survey responses.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-2)

Lorenz's work was interrupted by the onset of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), and in 1941 he was recruited into the [German Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Army_(1935%E2%80%931945) "German Army (1935–1945)") as a medic.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3) In 1944, he was sent to the [Eastern Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II) "Eastern Front (World War II)"), where he was captured by the Soviet [Red Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army "Red Army") and spent four years as a [German prisoner of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_prisoners_of_war_in_the_Soviet_Union "German prisoners of war in the Soviet Union") in [Soviet Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Armenia "Soviet Armenia"). After the war, he regretted his membership in the [Nazi Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Party "Nazi Party").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-4)

Lorenz wrote numerous books, some of which, such as _[King Solomon's Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Solomon's\_Ring\_(nonfiction) "King Solomon's Ring (nonfiction)")_, _[On Aggression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_Aggression "On Aggression")_, and _[Man Meets Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man\_Meets\_Dog "Man Meets Dog")_, became popular reading. His last work _Here I Am– Where Are You?_ is a summary of his life's work and focuses on his famous studies of greylag geese.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Lorenz was the son of [Adolf Lorenz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Lorenz "Adolf Lorenz"), a wealthy and distinguished surgeon, and his wife [Emma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Lorenz?action=edit&redlink=1 "Emma Lorenz (page does not exist)") (née Lecher), a physician who had been her husband's assistant.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-5) The family lived on a large estate at Altenberg and had a city apartment in Vienna.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-nytimes.com-6) He was educated at the [Public Schottengymnasium of the Benedictine monks in Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schottengymnasium "Schottengymnasium").

In his autobiographical essay, published in 1973 in _Les Prix Nobel_ (winners of the prizes are requested to provide such essays), Lorenz credits his career to his parents, who "were supremely tolerant of my inordinate love for animals", and to his childhood encounter with [Selma Lagerlöf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selma_Lagerl%C3%B6f "Selma Lagerlöf")'s _[The Wonderful Adventures of Nils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wonderful\_Adventures\_of\_Nils "The Wonderful Adventures of Nils")_, which filled him with a great enthusiasm about wild geese.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-7)

At the request of his father, he began a premedical curriculum in 1922 at [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-8) but returned to Vienna in 1923 to continue his studies at the [University of Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Vienna "University of Vienna"). He graduated as Doctor of Medicine (MD) in 1928 and became an assistant professor at the Institute of Anatomy until 1935. He finished his zoological studies in 1933 and received his second doctorate (PhD).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Routledge-9)

While still a student, Lorenz began developing what would become a large [menagerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menagerie "Menagerie"), ranging from domestic to exotic animals. In his popular book _[King Solomon's Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Solomon's\_Ring\_(nonfiction) "King Solomon's Ring (nonfiction)")_, Lorenz recounts that while studying at the University of Vienna, he kept a variety of animals at his parents' apartment, ranging from fish to a [capuchin monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capuchin_monkey "Capuchin monkey") named Gloria.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Routledge-9)

In 1936, at an international scientific symposium on instinct, Lorenz met his great friend and colleague [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen"). Together they studied [geese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geese "Geese")– wild, [domestic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_goose "Domestic goose"), and [hybrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamebird_hybrids#Goose_hybrids "Gamebird hybrids"). One result of these studies was that Lorenz "realized that an overpowering increase in the drives of feeding as well as of copulation and a waning of more differentiated social instincts is characteristic of very many domestic animals". Lorenz began to suspect and fear "that analogous processes of deterioration may be at work with civilized humanity". This observation of bird hybrids caused Lorenz to believe that domestication resulting from urbanisation in humans might also cause [dysgenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dysgenic "Dysgenic") effects, and to argue in two papers that the [Nazi eugenics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_eugenics "Nazi eugenics") policies against this were therefore scientifically justified.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-10)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Konrad_lorenz-rusky_lagr_1944-fotka.jpg/250px-Konrad_lorenz-rusky_lagr_1944-fotka.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Konrad_lorenz-rusky_lagr_1944-fotka.jpg)

Lorenz as a [Soviet POW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_prisoners_of_war_in_the_Soviet_Union "German prisoners of war in the Soviet Union") in 1944

In 1940 he became a professor of [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") at the [University of Königsberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_K%C3%B6nigsberg "University of Königsberg"). He was drafted into the [Wehrmacht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wehrmacht "Wehrmacht") in 1941. He sought to be a motorcycle mechanic, but instead he was assigned as a military psychologist, conducting racial studies on humans in occupied [Poznań](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pozna%C5%84 "Poznań") under [Rudolf Hippius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Hippius "Rudolf Hippius"). The objective was to study the biological characteristics of "German–Polish half-breeds" to determine whether they "benefited" from the same work ethics as "pure" Germans.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-12) The degree to which Lorenz participated in the project is unknown, but the project director Hippius referred a couple of times to Lorenz as an "examining psychologist".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-patterns-13)

Lorenz later described that he once saw transports of [concentration camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_concentration_camps "Nazi concentration camps") inmates at [Fort VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_VII "Fort VII") near [Poznań](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pozna%C5%84 "Poznań"), which made him "fully realize the complete inhumanity of the Nazis".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-14)

He was sent to the [Russian front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II) "Eastern Front (World War II)") in 1944, where he quickly became a [prisoner of war in the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_prisoners_of_war_in_the_Soviet_Union "German prisoners of war in the Soviet Union") from 1944 to 1948. In captivity in [Soviet Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Armenia "Soviet Armenia"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-15) he continued to work as a medic and "became tolerably fluent in Russian and got quite friendly with some Russians, mostly doctors".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-16) When he was repatriated, he was allowed to keep the manuscript of a book he had been writing and his pet [starling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starling "Starling"). He arrived back in Altenberg (his family home, near Vienna) both "with manuscript and bird intact". The manuscript became his 1973 book _[Behind the Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind\_the\_Mirror:\_A\_Search\_for\_a\_Natural\_History\_of\_Human\_Knowledge "Behind the Mirror: A Search for a Natural History of Human Knowledge")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)

The [Max Planck Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Society "Max Planck Society") established the Lorenz Institute for Behavioral Physiology in [Buldern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buldern "Buldern"), Germany, in 1950. In his memoirs, Lorenz described the chronology of his war years differently from what historians have been able to document after his death. He himself claimed that he was captured in 1942, where in reality he was only sent to the front and captured in 1944, leaving out entirely his involvement with the Poznań project.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)

In 1958, Lorenz transferred to the [Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Institute_for_Behavioral_Physiology "Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Physiology") in Seewiesen. He shared the 1973 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") "for discoveries in individual and social behavior patterns" with two other important early [ethologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethologists "Ethologists")–[Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen") and [Karl von Frisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_von_Frisch "Karl von Frisch"). In 1969, he became the first recipient of the [Prix mondial Cino Del Duca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prix_mondial_Cino_Del_Duca "Prix mondial Cino Del Duca"). He was a friend and student of renowned biologist [Sir Julian Huxley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Julian_Huxley "Sir Julian Huxley") (grandson of "Darwin's bulldog", [Thomas Henry Huxley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Henry_Huxley "Thomas Henry Huxley")). Famed psychoanalyst [Ralph Greenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Greenson "Ralph Greenson") and [Sir Peter Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Peter_Scott "Sir Peter Scott") were good friends. Lorenz and [Karl Popper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Popper "Karl Popper") were childhood friends; many years after they met, during the celebration of Popper's 80 years, they wrote together a book entitled _Die Zukunft ist offen_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-17)

He retired from the Max Planck Institute in 1973 but continued to research and publish from Altenberg and [Grünau im Almtal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnau_im_Almtal "Grünau im Almtal") in Austria. He died on 27 February 1989 in Altenberg.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Lorenz wed his childhood companion Margarethe Gebhardt, a gynaecologist and the daughter of a local market gardener.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-18) The couple had three children– one son and two daughters. He resided on the Lorenz family estate, notable for its "fantastical neo-baroque mansion", formally belonging to his father.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-nytimes.com-6)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-19)

## Ethology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Ethology")]

Further information: [Imprinting (psychology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(psychology) "Imprinting (psychology)") and [Ritualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ritualization "Ritualization")

Lorenz is recognized as one of the founding fathers of the field of [ethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethology "Ethology"), the study of animal behavior. He is best known for his research of the principle of attachment, or [imprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(psychology) "Imprinting (psychology)"), through which in some species a bond is formed between a newborn animal and its caregiver. This principle had been discovered by [Douglas Spalding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_Spalding "Douglas Spalding") in the 19th century, and Lorenz's mentor Oskar Heinroth had also worked on the topic, but Lorenz's description of _Prägung_, imprinting, in [nidifugous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nidifugous "Nidifugous") birds such as greylag geese in his 1935 book _Der Kumpan in der Umwelt des Vogels_ ("The Companion in the Environment of Birds") became the foundational description of the phenomenon.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-patterns-13)

Here, Lorenz used [Jakob von Uexküll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_von_Uexk%C3%BCll "Jakob von Uexküll")'s concept of _[Umwelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umwelt "Umwelt")_ to understand how the limited perception of animals filtered out certain phenomena with which they interacted instinctively. For example, a young goose instinctively bonds with the first moving stimulus it perceives, whether it be its mother, or a person. Lorenz showed that this behavior of [imprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(psychology) "Imprinting (psychology)") is what allows the goose to learn to recognize members of its own species, enabling them to be the object of subsequent behavior patterns such as mating.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-20) He developed a theory of instinctive behavior that saw behavior patterns as largely innate but triggered through environmental stimuli, for example, the [hawk/goose effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawk/goose_effect "Hawk/goose effect"). He argued that animals have an inner drive to carry out instinctive behaviors, and that if they do not encounter the right stimulus, they will eventually engage in the behavior with an inappropriate stimulus.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-21)

Lorenz's approach to ethology derived from a skepticism towards the studies of animal behavior done in laboratory settings. He considered that in order to understand the mechanisms of animal behavior, it was necessary to observe their full range of behaviors in their natural context. Lorenz did not carry out much traditional fieldwork but observed animals near his home. His method involved empathizing with animals, often using anthropomorphization to imagine their mental states. He believed that animals were capable of experiencing many of the same emotions as humans.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-20)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-22)

Tinbergen, Lorenz's friend with whom he conjointly received the Nobel Prize, summarized Lorenz's major contribution to ethology as making behavior a topic of biological inquiry, considering behavior a part of an animal's evolutionary equipment.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-23) Tinbergen and Lorenz contributed to making ethology a recognized sub-discipline within biology and founded the first specialized journal of the field "[Ethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethology_(journal) "Ethology (journal)")" (originally _Zeitschift für Tierpsychologie_).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-20)

## Involvement with Nazism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Involvement with Nazism")]

### Nazism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Nazism")]

Lorenz joined the [Nazi Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Socialist_German_Workers_Party "National Socialist German Workers Party") in 1938 and accepted a university chair under the [Nazi regime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"). In his application for party membership he wrote: "I'm able to say that my whole scientific work is devoted to the ideas of the [National Socialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazism "Nazism")." His publications during that time led in later years to allegations that his scientific work had been contaminated by Nazi sympathies. His published writing during the Nazi period included support for Nazi ideas of "[racial hygiene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_hygiene "Racial hygiene")" couched in [pseudoscientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudoscience "Pseudoscience") metaphors.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-29)

In his autobiography, Lorenz wrote:[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)

> The same individual geese on which we conducted these experiments, first aroused my interest in the process of domestication. They were [F1 hybrids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1_hybrid "F1 hybrid") of wild Greylags and domestic geese and they showed surprising deviations from the normal social and sexual behaviour of the wild birds. I realised that an overpowering increase in the drives of feeding as well as of copulation and a waning of more differentiated social instincts is characteristic of very many domestic animals. I was frightened– as I still am– by the thought that analogous genetical processes of deterioration may be at work with civilized humanity. Moved by this fear, I did a very ill-advised thing soon after the Germans had invaded Austria: I wrote about the dangers of domestication and, in order to be understood, I couched my writing in the worst of Nazi-terminology. I do not want to extenuate this action. I did, indeed, believe that some good might come of the new rulers. The precedent narrow-minded [Catholic regime in Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatherland_Front_(Austria) "Fatherland Front (Austria)") induced better and more intelligent men than I was to cherish this naive hope. Practically all my friends and teachers did so, including my own father who certainly was a kindly and humane man. None of us as much as suspected that the word "selection", when used by these rulers, meant murder. I regret those writings not so much for the undeniable discredit they reflect on my person as for their effect of hampering the future recognition of the dangers of domestication.

After the war, Lorenz denied having been a party member, until his membership application was made public,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-30) and he denied having known the extent of the genocide, despite his position as a psychologist in the [Office of Racial Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Racial_Policy "Office of Racial Policy").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-31) He was shown to have made [anti-Semitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Semitic "Anti-Semitic") jokes on "Jewish characteristics" in letters to his mentor Heinroth.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-32) In 2015, the [University of Salzburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Salzburg "University of Salzburg") posthumously rescinded an honorary doctorate awarded to Lorenz in 1983, citing his party membership and his assertions in his application that he was "always a National Socialist", and that his work "stands to serve National Socialist thought". The university also accused him of using his work to spread "basic elements of the racist ideology of National Socialism".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-FAZ_2015-34)

### Ecology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Ecology")]

During the final years of his life, Lorenz supported the fledgling [Austrian Green Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Green_Party "Austrian Green Party") and in 1984 became the figurehead of the Konrad Lorenz _[Volksbegehren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referendum "Referendum")_, a grass-roots movement that was formed to prevent the building of a [power plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_plant "Power plant") at the [Danube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube") near [Hainburg an der Donau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hainburg_an_der_Donau "Hainburg an der Donau") and thus the destruction of the surrounding woodland.

## Contributions and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Contributions and legacy")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Lorenz_and_Tinbergen1.jpg/250px-Lorenz_and_Tinbergen1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lorenz_and_Tinbergen1.jpg)

With [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen") (left), 1978

Lorenz has been called "The father of ethology" by Niko Tinbergen.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Tinbergen1963-35) Perhaps Lorenz's most important contribution to ethology was his idea that behavior patterns can be studied as anatomical organs.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Lorenz1937-36) This concept forms the foundation of ethological research.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Tinbergen1963-35)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Dawkins1982-37) However, [Richard Dawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dawkins "Richard Dawkins") called Lorenz a "'good of the species' man",[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Dawkins1976-38) stating that the idea of [group selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_selection "Group selection") was "so deeply ingrained"[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Dawkins1976-38) in Lorenz's thinking that he "evidently did not realize that his statements contravened [orthodox Darwinian theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Darwinism "Neo-Darwinism")".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Dawkins1976-38)

Together with [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen"), Lorenz developed the idea of an [innate releasing mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innate_releasing_mechanism "Innate releasing mechanism") to explain instinctive behaviors ([fixed action patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixed_action_pattern "Fixed action pattern")). They experimented with "[supernormal stimuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernormal_stimulus "Supernormal stimulus")" such as giant eggs or dummy bird beaks, which they found could release the fixed action patterns more powerfully than the natural objects for which the behaviors were adapted. Influenced by the ideas of [William McDougall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McDougall_(psychologist) "William McDougall (psychologist)"), Lorenz developed this into a "psychohydraulic" model of the [motivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motivation "Motivation") of behavior, which tended towards [group selectionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_selection "Group selection") ideas, which were influential in the 1960s. Another of his contributions to ethology is his work on [imprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprinting_(psychology) "Imprinting (psychology)"). His influence on a younger generation of [ethologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethologists "Ethologists") and his popular works were important in bringing ethology to the attention of the general public.

Lorenz claimed that there was widespread contempt for the descriptive sciences. He attributed this to the denial of perception as the source of all scientific knowledge: "a denial that has been elevated to the status of religion".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Lorenz1979-39) He wrote that in comparative behavioral research, "it is necessary to describe various patterns of movement, record them, and above all, render them unmistakably recognizable".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Lorenz1979p7-40)

There are three research institutions named after Lorenz in Austria: the [Konrad Lorenz Institute for Evolution and Cognition Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz_Institute_for_Evolution_and_Cognition_Research "Konrad Lorenz Institute for Evolution and Cognition Research") (KLI) was housed in Lorenz' family mansion at Altenberg before moving to [Klosterneuburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klosterneuburg "Klosterneuburg") in 2013; the [Konrad Lorenz Forschungsstelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz_Forschungsstelle "Konrad Lorenz Forschungsstelle") (KLF) at his former field station in Grünau; and the [Konrad Lorenz Institute of Ethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz_Institute_of_Ethology "Konrad Lorenz Institute of Ethology"), an external research facility of the [University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Veterinary_Medicine_Vienna "University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna").

### Vision of the challenges facing humanity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Vision of the challenges facing humanity")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Lorenz_and_Tinbergen2.jpg/250px-Lorenz_and_Tinbergen2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lorenz_and_Tinbergen2.jpg)

With Nikolaas Tinbergen (right), 1978

Lorenz predicted the relationship between market economics and the threat of ecological catastrophe. In his 1973 book _[Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilized\_Man's\_Eight\_Deadly\_Sins "Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins")_, Lorenz addresses the following paradox:[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Civilized-41):26

> All the advantages that man has gained from his ever-deepening understanding of the natural world that surrounds him, his technological, chemical and medical progress, all of which should seem to alleviate human suffering... tends instead to favor humanity's destruction.

Lorenz adopts an ecological model to attempt to grasp the mechanisms behind this contradiction. Thus "all species... are adapted to their environment... including not only inorganic components... but all the other living beings that inhabit the locality".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Civilized-41):31

Fundamental to Lorenz's theory of ecology is the function of [negative feedback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_feedback "Negative feedback") mechanisms, which, in hierarchical fashion, dampen impulses that occur beneath a certain threshold. The thresholds themselves are the product of the interaction of contrasting mechanisms. Thus pain and pleasure act as checks on each other:[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Civilized-41):53

> To gain a desired prey, a dog or wolf will do things that, in other contexts, they would shy away from: run through thorn bushes, jump into cold water and expose themselves to risks which would normally frighten them. All these inhibitory mechanisms... act as a counterweight to the effects of learning mechanisms... The organism cannot allow itself to pay a price which is not worth paying.

In nature, these mechanisms tend towards a "stable state" among the living beings of an ecology:[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Civilized-41):31–33

> A closer examination shows that these beings... not only do not damage each other, but often constitute a community of interests. It is obvious that the predator is strongly interested in the survival of that species, animal or vegetable, which constitutes its prey.... It is not uncommon that the prey species derives specific benefits from its interaction with the predator species...

Lorenz states that humanity is the one species not bound by these mechanisms, being the only one that has defined its own environment:[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Civilized-41)

> [The pace of human ecology] is determined by the progress of man's technology:35... human ecology (economy) is governed by mechanisms of _positive_ feedback, defined as a mechanism which tends to encourage behavior rather than to attenuate it.:43 Positive feedback always involves the danger of an "avalanche" effect... One particular kind of positive feedback occurs when individuals _of the same species_ enter into competition among themselves... For many animal species, environmental factors keep... intraspecies selection from [leading to] disaster... But there is no force which exercises this type of healthy regulatory effect on humanity's cultural development; unfortunately for itself, humanity has learned to overcome all those environmental forces which are external to itself.:44

Regarding aggression in human beings, Lorenz states:[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-On_Aggression-42):263

> Let us imagine that an absolutely unbiased investigator on another planet, perhaps on Mars, is examining human behavior on Earth, with the aid of a telescope whose magnification is too small to enable him to discern individuals and follow their separate behavior, but large enough for him to observe occurrences such as migrations of peoples, wars, and similar great historical events. He would never gain the impression that human behavior was dictated by intelligence, still less by responsible morality. If we suppose our extraneous observer to be a being of pure reason, devoid of instincts himself and unaware of the way in which all instincts in general and aggression in particular can miscarry, he would be at a complete loss how to explain history at all. The ever-recurrent phenomena of history do not have reasonable causes. It is a mere commonplace to say that they are caused by what common parlance so aptly terms "human nature". Unreasoning and unreasonable human nature causes two nations to compete, though no economic necessity compels them to do so; it induces two political parties or religions with amazingly similar programs of salvation to fight each other bitterly, and it impels an [Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great "Alexander the Great") or a [Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon") to sacrifice millions of lives in his attempt to unite the world under his scepter. We have been taught to regard some of the persons who have committed these and similar absurdities with respect, even as "great" men, we are wont to yield to the political wisdom of those in charge, and we are all so accustomed to these phenomena that most of us fail to realize how abjectly stupid and undesirable the historical mass behavior of humanity actually is.

Lorenz does not see human independence from natural ecological processes as necessarily bad. He states that:[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-On_Aggression-42):36

> A completely new [ecology] which corresponds in every way to [humanity's] desires... could, theoretically, prove as durable as that which would have existed without his intervention.

However, the principle of competition, typical of Western societies, destroys any chance of this:[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-On_Aggression-42):45–47

> The competition between human beings destroys with cold and diabolic brutality... Under the pressure of this competitive fury we have not only forgotten what is useful to humanity as a whole, but even that which is good and advantageous to the individual. [...] One asks, which is more damaging to modern humanity: the thirst for money or consuming haste... in either case, fear plays a very important role: the fear of being overtaken by one's competitors, the fear of becoming poor, the fear of making wrong decisions or the fear of not being up to snuff...

### Philosophical speculations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Philosophical speculations")]

In his 1973 book _[Behind the Mirror: A Search for a Natural History of Human Knowledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind\_the\_Mirror:\_A\_Search\_for\_a\_Natural\_History\_of\_Human\_Knowledge "Behind the Mirror: A Search for a Natural History of Human Knowledge")_, Lorenz considers the old philosophical question of whether our senses correctly inform us about the world as it is, or provide us only with an illusion. His answer comes from [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology "Evolutionary biology"). Only traits that help us survive and reproduce are transmitted. If our senses gave us wrong information about our environment, we would soon be extinct. Therefore, we can be sure that our senses give us correct information, for otherwise we would not be here to be deceived.

**Konrad Zacharias Lorenz** (pronunciación en alemán:[/ˈkɔnʁaːt ˈloːʁɛnts/](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayuda:AFI/Alem%C3%A1n "Ayuda:AFI/Alemán"); 7 de noviembre de 1903 – 27 de febrero de 1989), conocido como **Konrad Lorenz**, fue un [zoólogo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%B3logo "Zoólogo"), [etólogo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Et%C3%B3logo "Etólogo") y [ornitólogo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornit%C3%B3logo "Ornitólogo")[austríaco](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austr%C3%ADaco "Austríaco"). Compartió el [Premio Nobel de Medicina](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Nobel_de_Medicina "Premio Nobel de Medicina") de 1973 con [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen") y [Karl von Frisch](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_von_Frisch "Karl von Frisch"). A menudo se lo considera uno de los fundadores de la [etología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etolog%C3%ADa "Etología") moderna, el estudio del [comportamiento animal](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comportamiento_animal "Comportamiento animal") en su [hábitat](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A1bitat "Hábitat") natural. Desarrolló un enfoque que comenzó con una generación anterior, que incluía a su maestro [Oskar Heinroth](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskar_Heinroth "Oskar Heinroth").[[1]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-formemrs-1)

Lorenz estudió el comportamiento instintivo en animales, especialmente [gansos comunes](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anser_anser "Anser anser") y [grajillas occidentales](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloeus_monedula "Coloeus monedula"). Trabajando con gansos, investigó el principio de la [impronta](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impronta_(psicolog%C3%ADa) "Impronta (psicología)"), el proceso por el cual algunas aves [nidífugas](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nid%C3%ADfugas?action=edit&redlink=1 "Nidífugas (aún no redactado)") (es decir, aves que abandonan su nido temprano) se unen instintivamente con el primer objeto en movimiento que ven dentro de las primeras horas de la [eclosión](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclosi%C3%B3n "Eclosión") de sus huevos. Aunque Lorenz no descubrió el tema, se hizo ampliamente conocido por sus descripciones de la impronta como un vínculo instintivo. En 1936 conoció a Tinbergen, y los dos colaboraron en el desarrollo de la etología como una subdisciplina separada de la biología.

Un estudio del _Review of General Psychology_, publicado en el 2002, clasificó a Lorenz como el 65.º erudito más citado del siglo XX en las [revistas científicas](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revistas_cient%C3%ADficas "Revistas científicas") de [psicología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psicolog%C3%ADa "Psicología"), manuales universitarios introductorios de psicología y reseñas de estudios.[[2]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-2)

El trabajo de Lorenz fue interrumpido por el inicio de la [Segunda Guerra Mundial](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Guerra_Mundial "Segunda Guerra Mundial") y en 1941 fue reclutado en el [ejército alemán](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ej%C3%A9rcito_alem%C3%A1n "Ejército alemán") como médico.[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3) En 1944 fue enviado al [Frente Oriental](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frente_oriental_(Segunda_Guerra_Mundial) "Frente oriental (Segunda Guerra Mundial)"), donde fue capturado por el [Ejército Rojo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ej%C3%A9rcito_Rojo "Ejército Rojo") y pasó cuatro años como [prisionero de guerra](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisionero_de_guerra "Prisionero de guerra") alemán en la Armenia soviética. Durante estos años, fue miembro del [Partido Nacionalsocialista Obrero Alemán](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_Nacionalsocialista_Obrero_Alem%C3%A1n "Partido Nacionalsocialista Obrero Alemán") (Partido Nazi).[[4]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-4)

Lorenz escribió numerosos libros, algunos de los cuales, como _El anillo del rey Salomón_, _[Sobre la agresión](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobre\_la\_agresi%C3%B3n "Sobre la agresión")_ y _El hombre se encuentra con el perro_, se convirtieron en lecturas populares.

## Biografía

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=1 "Editar sección: Biografía")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Lorenz_1904.jpg/250px-Lorenz_1904.jpg?utm_source=es.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archivo:Lorenz_1904.jpg)

Junto a su padre Alfred Lorenz en 1904.

### Primeros años y estudios (1903-1933)

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=2 "Editar sección: Primeros años y estudios (1903-1933)")]

En su [ensayo autobiográfico](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiograf%C3%ADa "Autobiografía"), publicado en 1973 en _Les Prix Nobel_ (se solicita a los ganadores de los premios que proporcionen dichos ensayos), Lorenz acredita su carrera a sus padres, quienes "fueron sumamente tolerantes con mi excesivo amor por los animales", y también, al encuentro durante su infancia con _[El maravilloso viaje de Nils Holgersson](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_maravilloso\_viaje\_de\_Nils\_Holgersson "El maravilloso viaje de Nils Holgersson")_ de [Selma Lagerlöf](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selma_Lagerl%C3%B6f "Selma Lagerlöf"), que "lo llenó de un gran entusiasmo por los gansos salvajes".[[5]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-5)

A pedido de su padre, Adolf Lorenz, comenzó a estudiar su pregrado en [medicina](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicina "Medicina") en 1922 en la [Universidad de Columbia](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_Columbia "Universidad de Columbia"), pero regresó a Viena en 1923 para continuar sus estudios en la [Universidad de Viena](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_Viena "Universidad de Viena"). Se graduó como [doctor en Medicina](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_en_Medicina "Doctor en Medicina")(M.D.) en 1928 y se convirtió en profesor asistente en su Instituto de Anatomía hasta 1935. Comenzó un segundo [doctorado](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctorado "Doctorado")([Ph.D.](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ph.D. "Ph.D.")), esta vez en [zoología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoolog%C3%ADa "Zoología"), del cual egresó en 1933.[[6]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Routledge-6)

Mientras todavía era estudiante, Lorenz comenzó a construir lo que se convertiría en una gran [ménagerie](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9nagerie "Ménagerie") («casa de fieras»), desde animales domésticos hasta animales exóticos. En su popular libro _El anillo del rey Salomón_, Lorenz cuenta que mientras estudiaba en la [Universidad de Viena](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_Viena "Universidad de Viena") mantuvo una variedad de animales en el departamento de sus padres, desde peces hasta un [mono capuchino](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mono_capuchino "Mono capuchino") llamado Gloria.[[6]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Routledge-6)

### Inicios como académico (1933-1939)

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=3 "Editar sección: Inicios como académico (1933-1939)")]

En 1936, en un simposio científico internacional sobre el [instinto](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinto "Instinto"), Lorenz conoció a su gran amigo y colega [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen"). Juntos estudiaron gansos: salvajes, domésticos e híbridos. Un resultado de estos estudios fue que Lorenz "se dio cuenta de que un aumento abrumador en los impulsos de alimentación, así como de la cópula y una disminución de los instintos sociales más diferenciados es característica de muchos animales domésticos". Lorenz comenzó a sospechar y temer "que procesos análogos de deterioro puedan estar trabajando con la humanidad civilizada". Esta observación de los híbridos de aves hizo que Lorenz creyera que la domesticación resultante de la urbanización en humanos también podría causar efectos disgénicos, y argumentar en dos artículos que las [políticas eugenésicas nazis](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenesia_nazi "Eugenesia nazi") contra esto, por lo tanto, estaban científicamente justificadas.[[7]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-7)

### Participación en la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-1948)

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=4 "Editar sección: Participación en la Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-1948)")]

En 1940 se convirtió en profesor de psicología en la [Universidad de Königsberg](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_K%C3%B6nigsberg "Universidad de Königsberg"). Fue reclutado en la [Wehrmacht](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wehrmacht "Wehrmacht") en 1941. Intentó ser mecánico de motocicletas, pero en su lugar fue asignado como psicólogo militar, realizando estudios raciales sobre humanos en la Poznań ocupada bajo [Rudolf Hippius](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Hippius?action=edit&redlink=1 "Rudolf Hippius (aún no redactado)"). El objetivo era estudiar las características biológicas de las "[mestizos](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mestizo "Mestizo")[alemanes](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alemanes_%C3%A9tnicos "Alemanes étnicos")-[polacos](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_polaco "Pueblo polaco")" para determinar si se "beneficiaban" de la misma ética de trabajo que los [alemanes puros](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alemanes_%C3%A9tnicos "Alemanes étnicos").[[8]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-9) Se desconoce el grado en que Lorenz participó en el proyecto, pero el director del proyecto Hippius se refirió un par de veces a Lorenz como el "[psicólogo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psic%C3%B3logo "Psicólogo") examinador".[[10]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-patterns-10)

Más tarde, Lorenz declaró que una vez vio transportes de reclusos en [campos de concentración](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campo_de_concentraci%C3%B3n "Campo de concentración") en el Fuerte VII cerca de [Poznań](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pozna%C5%84 "Poznań"), lo que lo hizo «darse cuenta por completo de la completa inhumanidad de los nazis».[[11]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-11)

Fue enviado al frente ruso en 1944, donde rápidamente se convirtió en [prisionero de guerra](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisionero_de_guerra "Prisionero de guerra") en la [Unión Soviética](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uni%C3%B3n_Sovi%C3%A9tica "Unión Soviética") de 1944 a 1948. En cautiverio en la [Armenia soviética](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia_sovi%C3%A9tica "Armenia soviética"),[[12]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-12) continuó trabajando como médico y «se hizo tolerablemente fluido en ruso y se hizo bastante amigable con algunos rusos, en su mayoría médicos».[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3) Cuando fue repatriado, se le permitió conservar el manuscrito de un libro que había estado escribiendo y su [estornino](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estornino "Estornino") mascota. Llegó a Altenberg (la casa de su familia, cerca de Viena) tanto "con el manuscrito como con el pájaro intacto". El manuscrito se convirtió en su libro de 1973 _Die Rückseite des Spiegels_.[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)

### Regreso a Viena, Premio Nobel de Medicina y últimos años (1949-1989)

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=5 "Editar sección: Regreso a Viena, Premio Nobel de Medicina y últimos años (1949-1989)")]

La [Sociedad Max Planck](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedad_Max_Planck "Sociedad Max Planck") estableció el "Instituto Lorenz de Fisiología del Comportamiento" en Buldern, Alemania, en 1950. En sus memorias, Lorenz describió la cronología de sus años de guerra de manera diferente de lo que los historiadores han podido documentar después de su muerte. Él mismo afirmó que fue capturado en 1942, donde en realidad solo fue enviado al frente y capturado en 1944, dejando completamente de lado su participación en el proyecto de Poznań.[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)

En 1958, Lorenz se transfirió al [Instituto Max Planck](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Max_Planck "Instituto Max Planck") de Fisiología del Comportamiento en Seewiesen. Compartió el [Premio Nobel de Fisiología o Medicina](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Nobel_de_Fisiolog%C3%ADa_o_Medicina "Premio Nobel de Fisiología o Medicina") de 1973 "por descubrimientos en patrones de comportamiento individual y social" con otros dos importantes etólogos tempranos, [Nikolaas Tinbergen](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolaas_Tinbergen "Nikolaas Tinbergen") y [Karl von Frisch](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_von_Frisch "Karl von Frisch"). En 1969, se convirtió en el primer receptor del [Premio Mundial Cino Del Duca](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Mundial_Cino_Del_Duca "Premio Mundial Cino Del Duca"). Era amigo y alumno del reconocido biólogo Sir [Julian Huxley](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Huxley "Julian Huxley") (nieto del "bulldog de Darwin", [Thomas Henry Huxley](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Henry_Huxley "Thomas Henry Huxley"), y hermano del escritor [Aldous Huxley](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldous_Huxley "Aldous Huxley")). El famoso psicoanalista [Ralph Greenson](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Greenson "Ralph Greenson") y Sir [Peter Scott](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Scott "Peter Scott") eran buenos amigos suyos. Lorenz y [Karl Popper](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Popper "Karl Popper") eran amigos de la infancia. Muchos años después de conocerse, durante la celebración de los 80 años de Popper, escribieron juntos un libro titulado _Die Zukunft ist offen_.[[13]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-13)

Se retiró del [Instituto Max Planck](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Max_Planck "Instituto Max Planck") en 1973, pero continuó investigando y publicando en Altenberg y Grünau im Almtal en Austria. Murió el 27 de febrero de 1989 en Altenberg.

## Etología

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=6 "Editar sección: Etología")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Alserstr.4_AKH_Path.Anatom.Institut_1154.JPG/250px-Alserstr.4_AKH_Path.Anatom.Institut_1154.JPG?utm_source=es.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archivo:Alserstr.4_AKH_Path.Anatom.Institut_1154.JPG)

Facultad de Medicina de la [Universidad de Viena](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_Viena "Universidad de Viena").

Lorenz es reconocido como uno de los padres fundadores del campo de la [etología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etolog%C3%ADa "Etología"), el estudio del comportamiento animal en su [hábitat](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A1bitat "Hábitat") natural. Es conocido por su descubrimiento del principio de apego o [impronta](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impronta_(psicolog%C3%ADa) "Impronta (psicología)"), a través del cual en algunas especies se forma un vínculo entre un animal recién nacido y su cuidador. [Douglas Spalding](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_Spalding?action=edit&redlink=1 "Douglas Spalding (aún no redactado)") descubrió este principio en el siglo XIX, y el mentor de Lorenz, [Oskar Heinroth](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskar_Heinroth "Oskar Heinroth"), también había trabajado en el tema, pero la descripción de Lorenz de _Prägung_, impronta, en pájaros nidifugos como los gansos grises en su libro de 1935 _Der Kumpan en der Umwelt des Vogels_ ("El compañero en el medio ambiente de las aves") devino en explicación fundamental del fenómeno.[[10]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-patterns-10)

Aquí, Lorenz especificó el concepto de _[Umwelt](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umwelt?action=edit&redlink=1 "Umwelt (aún no redactado)")_ de [Jakob von Uexküll](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_von_Uexk%C3%BCll "Jakob von Uexküll") para comprender cómo la percepción limitada de los animales filtraba ciertos fenómenos con los que interactúan instintivamente. Por ejemplo, un joven ganso se une instintivamente con el primer estímulo móvil que percibe, ya sea su madre o una persona. Lorenz demostró que este comportamiento de impronta es lo que le permite al ganso aprender a reconocer a los miembros de su propia especie, lo que les permite ser objeto de patrones de comportamiento posterior, como el apareamiento.[[14]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-14) Desarrolló una teoría del comportamiento instintivo que considera que los patrones de comportamiento son, en gran medida, innatos, pero que se activan a través de estímulos ambientales (como por ejemplo, el _efecto halcón/ganso_). Argumentó que los animales tienen un impulso interno para llevar a cabo los comportamientos instintivos, y si no encuentran el estímulo correcto, finalmente se involucrarán en el comportamiento con un estímulo inapropiado.[[15]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-15)

El enfoque de Lorenz a la etología proviene de un escepticismo hacia los estudios de comportamiento animal realizados en entornos de laboratorio. Él consideraba que, para comprender los mecanismos del comportamiento animal, era necesario observar su gama completa de comportamientos en su contexto natural. Lorenz no realizó mucho trabajo de campo tradicional pero detectó animales cerca de su casa. Su método implicaba empatizar con los animales, a menudo usando la antropomorfización para imaginar sus estados mentales. Él creía que los animales experimentan fácilmente muchas de las mismas emociones "humanas".[[14]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-14)[[16]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-16)

Tinbergen, amigo de Lorenz con quien recibió el premio Nobel, resumió la importante contribución de Lorenz a la etología como hacer del comportamiento un tema de investigación biológica, el comportamiento como parte del equipo evolutivo de un animal.[[17]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-17) Tinbergen y Lorenz contribuyeron a hacer de la [Etología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etolog%C3%ADa "Etología") una subdisciplina reconocida dentro de la [Biología](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biolog%C3%ADa "Biología") y crearon el primer journal académico especializado en este nuevo campo: "Ethology" (originalmente llamado "Zeitschift für Tierpsychologie")[[14]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-species-14)

## Postura política: nazismo y ecología

[[editar](https://es.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=7 "Editar sección: Postura política: nazismo y ecología")]

Lorenz se unió al [Partido Nazi](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_Nazi "Partido Nazi") en 1938 y aceptó una cátedra universitaria bajo el [régimen nazi](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tercer_Reich "Tercer Reich"). En su solicitud para ser miembro del partido, escribió: "Puedo decir que todo mi trabajo científico está consagrado a las ideas de los [nacionalsocialistas](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalsocialistas "Nacionalsocialistas")". Sus publicaciones durante ese tiempo llevaron en años posteriores a acusaciones de que su trabajo científico había sido contaminado por simpatías [nazis](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi "Nazi"). Su trabajos publicados durante el período nazi incluyó el apoyo a las ideas nazis de "[higiene racial](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higiene_racial "Higiene racial")".[[18]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-23)

En su autobiografía, Lorenz escribió:

> _I was frightened—as I still am—by the thought that analogous genetical processes of deterioration may be at work with civilized humanity. Moved by this fear, I did a very ill-advised thing soon after the Germans had invaded Austria: I wrote about the dangers of domestication and, in order to be understood, I couched my writing in the worst of Nazi terminology. I do not want to extenuate this action. I did, indeed, believe that some good might come of the new rulers. The precedent narrow-minded catholic regime in Austria induced better and more intelligent men than I was to cherish this naive hope. Practically all my friends and teachers did so, including my own father who certainly was a kindly and humane man. None of us as much as suspected that the word "selection", when used by these rulers, meant murder. I regret those writings not so much for the undeniable discredit they reflect on my person as for their effect of hampering the future recognition of the dangers of human domestication._[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)  
>   
> Estaba asustado, como todavía lo estoy, por la idea de que [procesos genéticos análogos de deterioro](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disgenesia "Disgenesia") puedan estar desarrollándose como producto de la humanidad civilizada. Movido por este miedo, hice algo muy poco aconsejable poco después de que los alemanes habían invadido Austria: escribí sobre los peligros de la [domesticación](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesticaci%C3%B3n "Domesticación") y, para que me entendieran, redacté mis escritos con la peor terminología [nazi](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi "Nazi"). No quiero atenuar esta acción. De hecho, creía que algo bueno podría venir de [los nuevos gobernantes](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler"). El régimen católico de mente estrecha precedente en Austria indujo a mejores y más inteligentes hombres que yo a apreciar esta ingenua esperanza. Prácticamente todos mis amigos y maestros lo hicieron, incluido mi propio padre, que ciertamente era un hombre amable y humano. Ninguno de nosotros sospechaba que la palabra "selección", utilizada por estos gobernantes, significaba [asesinato](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asesinato "Asesinato"). Lamento esos escritos no tanto por el innegable descrédito que reflejan en mi persona como por su efecto de obstaculizar el reconocimiento futuro de los peligros de la [domesticación](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesticaci%C3%B3n "Domesticación") humana.[[3]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Nobelprize.org-3)
> 
> 
> 
> Konrad Lorenz, 1973

Cuando se hizo pública su solicitud de membresía, negó haber sabido el alcance del [genocidio](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocidio "Genocidio"), a pesar de su posición como [psicólogo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psic%C3%B3logo "Psicólogo") en la [Oficina de Política Racial](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oficina_de_Pol%C3%ADticas_Raciales_del_NSDAP "Oficina de Políticas Raciales del NSDAP").[[24]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Sin-nombre-p2Ry-1-24)[[25]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-25)

También se demostró que había hecho bromas [antisemitas](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemita "Antisemita") sobre 'características judías' en cartas a su mentor Heinroth.[[24]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-Sin-nombre-p2Ry-1-24) En 2015, la [Universidad de Salzburgo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_de_Salzburgo "Universidad de Salzburgo") rescindió póstumamente un doctorado honorario otorgado a Lorenz en 1983, citando su membresía del partido y sus afirmaciones en dicha solicitud, a saber, que fue "desde siempre un [nacionalsocialista](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalsocialista "Nacionalsocialista")", y que su trabajo "está al servicio del pensamiento nacionalsocialista". La universidad también lo acusó de utilizar su trabajo para difundir "elementos básicos de la ideología [racista](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racista "Racista") del [nacionalsocialismo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalsocialismo "Nacionalsocialismo")".[[26]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Lorenz#cite_note-FAZ_2015-27)

Durante los últimos años de su vida, Lorenz apoyó al incipiente [Partido Verde de Austria](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Verdes-La_Alternativa_Verde "Los Verdes-La Alternativa Verde") y en 1984 se convirtió en la cara visible del _Konrad Lorenz Volksbegehren_, un [movimiento de base](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grassroots "Grassroots") que se formó para evitar la construcción de una planta de energía en el Danubio cerca de Hainburg an der Donau y, por lo tanto, la destrucción del bosque circundante.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Konrad_Lorenz.JPG/250px-Konrad_Lorenz.JPG?utm_source=en.wikiquote.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/File:Konrad_Lorenz.JPG)

Far from seeing in man the irrevocable and unsurpassable image of God, I assert – more modestly and, I believe, in greater awe of the Creation and its infinite possibilities – that the long-sought missing link between animals and the really humane being is ourselves!

**[Konrad Zacharias Lorenz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad%20Lorenz "w:Konrad Lorenz")** ([November 7](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/November_7 "November 7"), [1903](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/1903 "1903") – [February 27](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/February_27 "February 27"), [1989](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/1989 "1989")) was an Austrian zoologist, animal psychologist, and ornithologist. He is one of the recipients of the 1973 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel%20Prize%20in%20Physiology%20or%20Medicine "w:Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine"). He is often regarded as one of the founders of modern [ethology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ethology "w:ethology").

## Quotes

[[edit](https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Quotes")]

*   The same individual geese on which we conducted these experiments, first aroused my interest in the process of domestication. They were F1 hybrids of wild Greylags and domestic geese and they showed surprising deviations from the normal social and sexual behaviour of the wild birds. I realised that an overpowering increase in the drives of feeding as well as of copulation and a waning of more differentiated social instincts is characteristic of very many domestic animals. I was frightened – as I still am – by the thought that analogous genetical processes of deterioration may be at work with civilized humanity. Moved by this fear, I did a very ill-advised thing soon after the Germans had invaded Austria: I wrote about the dangers of domestication and, in order to be understood, I couched my writing in the worst of nazi-terminology. I do not want to extenuate this action. I did, indeed, believe that some good might come of the new rulers. The precedent narrow-minded catholic regime in Austria induced better and more intelligent men than I was to cherish this naive hope. Practically all my friends and teachers did so, including my own father who certainly was a kindly and humane man. None of us as much as suspected that the word "selection", when used by these rulers, meant murder. I regret those writings not so much for the undeniable discredit they reflect on my person as for their effect of hampering the future recognition of **the dangers of domestication.**
    *   [_Konrad Lorenz Biographical_](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1973/lorenz/biographical/), The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1973.

### _[On Aggression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On%20Aggression "w:On Aggression")_ (1963)

[[edit](https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section:  On Aggression (1963)")]

*   It is a good morning exercise for a research scientist to discard a pet hypothesis every day before breakfast. It keeps him young. 
    *   Trans. M. Latzke (1966), p. 8

*   **All too willingly man sees himself as the centre of the universe, as something not belonging to the rest of nature but standing apart as a different and higher being. Many people cling to this error and remain deaf to the wisest command ever given by a sage, the famous "[Know thyself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Know%20thyself "w:Know thyself")" inscribed in the temple of Delphi.**
    *   [Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility](https://www.marxists.org/reference/subject/philosophy/works/ge/lorenz.htm)

*   The scientist who considers himself absolutely "objective" and believes that he can free himself from the compulsion of the "merely" subjective should try — only in imagination of course — to kill in succession a lettuce, a fly, a frog, a guineapig, a cat, a dog, and finally a chimpanzee. He will then be aware how increasingly difficult murder becomes as the victim's level of organisation rises. The degree of inhibition against killing each one of these beings is a very precise measure for the considerably different values that we cannot help attributing to lower and higher forms of life. To any man who finds it equally easy to chop up a live dog and a live lettuce I would recommend suicide at his earliest convenience! 
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   **We are the highest achievement reached so far by the great constructors of evolution. We are their "latest" but certainly not their last word.** The scientist must not regard anything as absolute, not even the laws of pure reason. He must remain aware of the great fact, discovered by [Heraclitus](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Heraclitus "Heraclitus"), that nothing whatever really remains the same even for one moment, but that everything is perpetually changing. **To regard man, the most ephemeral and rapidly evolving of all species, as the final and unsurpassable achievement of creation, especially at his present-day particularly dangerous and disagreeable stage of development, is certainly the most arrogant and dangerous of all untenable doctrines. If I thought of man as the final image of God, I should not know what to think of God.** But when I consider that our ancestors, at a time fairly recent in relation to the earth's history, were perfectly ordinary apes, closely related to chimpanzees, I see a glimmer of hope. **It does not require very great optimism to assume that from us human beings something better and higher may evolve. Far from seeing in man the irrevocable and unsurpassable image of God, I assert – more modestly and, I believe, in greater awe of the Creation and its infinite possibilities – that the long-sought missing link between animals and the really humane being is ourselves!**
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   Nobody can seriously believe that free will means that it is left entirely to the will of the individual, as to an irresponsible tyrant, to do or not do whatever he pleases. **Our freest will underlies strict moral laws, and one of the reasons for our longing for freedom is to prevent our obeying other laws than these.** It is significant that the anguished feeling of not being free is never evoked by the realisation that our behaviour is just as firmly bound to moral laws as physiological processes are to physical ones. We are all agreed that the greatest and most precious freedom of man is identical with the moral laws within him. Increasing knowledge of the natural causes of his own behaviour can certainly increase a man's faculties and enable him to put his free will into action, but it can never diminish his will. If, in the impossible case of an utopian complete and ultimate success of causal analysis, man should ever achieve complete insight into the causality of earthly phenomena, including the workings of his own organism, he would not cease to have a will but it would be in perfect harmony with the incontrovertible lawfulness of the universe, the _Weltvernunft_ of the [Logos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logos "w:Logos"). This idea is foreign only to our present-day western thought; it was quite familiar to ancient [Indian philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian%20philosophy "w:Indian philosophy") and to the mystics of the middle ages. 
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   I now come to the third great obstacle to human self-knowledge, to the belief — deeply rooted in our western culture — that what can be explained in terms of natural science has no values. This belief springs from an exaggeration of [Kant](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Immanuel_Kant "Immanuel Kant")'s values-philosophy, the consequence of the idealistic dichotomy of the world into the external world of things and the internal laws of human reason. 
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   The attitude of the true scientist towards the real limits of human understanding was unforgettably impressed on me in early youth by the obviously unpremeditated words of a great biologist; [Alfred Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred%20Kuhn "w:Alfred Kuhn") finished a lecture to the Austrian Academy of Science with [Goethe](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Goethe "Goethe")'s words, "It is the greatest joy of the man of thought to have explored the explorable and then calmly to revere the inexplorable." After the last word he hesitated, raised his hand in repudiation and cried, above the applause, "No, not calmly, gentlemen; not _calmly_!" 
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   Nothing can better express the feelings of the scientist towards the great unity of the laws of nature than in [Immanuel Kant](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Immanuel_Kant "Immanuel Kant")'s words: "Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing awe: the stars above me and the moral law within me."… Would he, who did not yet know of the evolution of the world of organisms, be shocked that we consider the moral law within us not as something given, a priori, but as something which has arisen by natural evolution, just like the laws of the heavens? 
    *   Ch. XII: On the Virtue of Scientific Humility

*   Let us imagine that an absolutely unbiased investigator on another planet, perhaps on Mars, is examining human behavior on earth, with the aid of a telescope whose magnification is too small to enable him to discern individuals and follow their separate behavior, but large enough for him to observe occurrences such as migrations of peoples, wars, and similar great historical events. He would never gain the impression that human behavior was dictated by intelligence, still less by responsible morality. 
    *   Ch. XIII: Ecce Homo!

### _Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins_ (1973)

[[edit](https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=Konrad_Lorenz&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins (1973)")]

*   All the advantages that man has gained from his ever-deepening understanding of the natural world that surrounds him, his technological, chemical and medical progress, all of which should seem to alleviate human suffering... tends instead to favor humanity's destruction.

*   **The competition between human beings destroys with cold and diabolic brutality.... Under the pressure of this competitive fury we have not only forgotten what is useful to humanity as a whole, but even that which is good and advantageous to the individual....** One asks, which is more damaging to modern humanity: the thirst for money or consuming haste... in either case, fear plays a very important role: the fear of being overtaken by one's competitors, the fear of becoming poor, the fear of making wrong decisions or the fear of not being up to snuff. 
    *   pp 45-47
